clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old previously healthy White infant presented with a 7-day history of photophobia, eye blinking, rubbing, irritability, and decreased oral intake. Ophthalmologic examination revealed bilateral dendritiform corneal lesions, significant photophobia, epiphora, and difficulty maintaining eyelids open, initially raising suspicion for herpetic keratitis given the mother's history of cold sores. A papular, crusted, raised lesion was noted on the thumb. HSV PCR testing on conjunctival swab and thumb lesion was negative, ruling out herpetic infection. Metabolic workup revealed markedly elevated plasma tyrosine level of 1262 µmol/L (normal reference range 40–80 µmol/L), confirming the diagnosis of tyrosinemia type II (TYRII). The bilateral dendritiform corneal lesions and cutaneous manifestations represent tyrosine-related oculocutaneous findings rather than HSV infection. Dietary treatment was initiated, and after 2 weeks of treatment, the plasma tyrosine level decreased to 152 µmol/L (mildly elevated), with no recurrence of corneal lesions.

final.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old previously healthy White infant presented with a 7-day history of photophobia, eye blinking, rubbing, irritability, and decreased oral intake. Ophthalmologic examination revealed bilateral dendritiform corneal lesions, significant photophobia, epiphora, and difficulty maintaining eyelids open, initially raising suspicion for herpetic keratitis given the mother's history of cold sores. A papular, crusted, raised lesion was noted on the thumb. HSV PCR testing on conjunctival swab and thumb lesion was negative, ruling out herpetic infection. Metabolic workup revealed markedly elevated plasma tyrosine level of 1262 µmol/L (normal reference range 40–80 µmol/L), confirming the diagnosis of tyrosinemia type II (TYRII). The bilateral dendritiform corneal lesions and cutaneous manifestations represent tyrosine-related oculocutaneous findings rather than HSV infection. Dietary treatment was initiated, and after 2 weeks of treatment, the plasma tyrosine level decreased to 152 µmol/L (mildly elevated), with no recurrence of corneal lesions.
